blocks.text:
## Ecuador on Foot, by Raft and Among Volcanoes

The altitude, climate and scenery change as you travel. Quito’s colonial streets give way to cloud forest, followed by high-altitude wetlands, crater lakes, rocky peaks and volcanoes. In Mindo, you may hear woodpeckers and see hummingbirds. On the trails around Cotopaxi and Chimborazo, you may spot alpacas and vicuñas, and in Baños you’ll spend a day among waterfalls and hot springs.

This is an active itinerary, with hikes lasting up to 6–7 hours, elevations of up to 5,000 m, ziplining, an opportunity to go tubing, class IV–IV+ rafting and several long transfers. The schedule leaves time to recover at lodges and hot spring resorts after strenuous activities. The changes are especially striking in the mountains. In a single day you can go from a humid valley to the cold highlands and then see a line of volcanoes from an open trail. The trip calls for a good level of fitness, with a different activity and landscape almost every day.
